rule: Each single-colour cup (closed on three sides, open on one) holds marker cells of another colour. Erase the markers. Then draw a line of the marker colour, with length equal to the marker count, outward from the cup's extreme cell on the closed side, opposite the opening. Clip the line at the grid border.
scope: Erase cup markers and draw an outward line on the closed side with length equal to marker count, clipped to the grid. Random canvases 9..30, one to four distinct-colour cups, U and vertical/diagonal arch shapes, four orientations, one to fifteen markers subject to enclosure capacity. Exact cup count, shape family and marker count are controllable.

authored_scope: Random scenes have 1-3 cups of distinct colours on a black background, in grids of 9..18 per side. Each cup is a rotated U shape with interior width 1-4 and depth 1-4. Wall heights are unequal and random. Corners may be cut diagonally and wall tops may be flared. A 1-2 cell knob on the closed side makes the start cell unique. Each cup holds 1-7 interior markers of one colour, which may equal another cup's colour. There are 0-3 lone distractor cells outside all cups. Lines are frequently clipped. Not supported in random mode: irregular arch or chevron outlines, markers outside the cup interior where some closed-side rays escape, multi-colour markers within one cup, same-colour cups, and non-black backgrounds. The original fixtures, which use those irregular shapes, are reproduced only through explicit latent container specs.
authored_constraints: Cup bounding boxes plus their drawn line paths are separated from each other and from distractors by at least one cell (Chebyshev).
Only the cup and its markers lie inside each cup's bounding box.
From every marker, the ray in the opening direction never meets the cup colour anywhere in the grid. The other directions' escape counts are strictly smaller, so the opening is unambiguous.
Each cup has strictly more cells than it has markers, and distractors are single cells, so cups are processed before marker or distractor components.
The extreme cell on the closed side is unique because of the knob.
At least one line cell is drawn inside the grid, so every sample is nonidentity.
Black (0) is strictly the most frequent colour.
